title: The Copper Scroll
subtitle: Qumran Cave 3 · 1952
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, the Judean desert by the Dead Sea: pale limestone cliffs and caves and an ancient corroded copper scroll, warm low lamplight against dusty ochre and bronze-green, quiet and uncanny, ancient detail, cinematic vertical composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Qumran, nineteen fifty-two. In a cave by the Dead Sea, archaeologists found a scroll made of copper.
beats.img: Two rolled cylinders of ancient corroded copper sheet, green-brown patina, rows of small engraved marks visible along the curled edges, resting centred on a flat pale limestone ledge inside a cave, lit by a warm low lamp from one side, sharp detail, the object filling the middle of a tall vertical frame, dark soft cave wall behind.

beats.vo: It is a list. Sixty-four hiding places, and the treasure said to lie at nearly all of them.
beats.img: Extreme close-up of a curved strip of corroded ancient copper with neat rows of small hand-engraved characters, worn and illegible, green and bronze oxide, raking warm light catching the incised grooves, vertical composition.

beats.vo: It was sawn into strips to be read. By some estimates, the total runs to tons.
beats.img: Many narrow curved segments of corroded green copper laid side by side in neat rows on dark cloth on a stone ledge inside a cave, lit from above by a single warm lamp, quiet and exact, vertical composition.

beats.vo: In the early nineteen-sixties, an expedition dug at some of the sites. It found nothing. No treasure has ever been found.
beats.img: A dry desert ravine below pale limestone cliffs at dusk, a few old shallow excavation pits and spoil heaps in the gravel, abandoned and empty, long shadows, tall vertical composition.

beats.vo: Temple treasure hidden from Rome, a legend, or a hoax? Scholars still disagree.
beats.img: A dark cave mouth high in a weathered limestone cliff at dusk, the hazy flat surface of the Dead Sea far below, empty and silent, tall vertical composition.

facts.claim: Found March 1952 by archaeologists at the back of Qumran Cave 3, near the Dead Sea; made of copper (with ~1% tin)
Too brittle to unroll; H. Wright Baker at Manchester sawed it into 23 strips in 1955–56, after which it was read/translated
It lists 64 hiding places of gold, silver and other treasure (63 with gold/silver)
Totals vary by translation/estimate (~4,500 talents; estimates 'in tons'; NCRegister ~65 t gold + 26 t silver; others 58–174 t) — hence 'by some estimates, tons'
John Allegro's 1962 expedition dug at some listed sites and found nothing; none of the treasure has ever been found (still none as of July 2026)
Theories: Second Temple treasure hidden from the Romans, Bar Kokhba hoard, legendary/folklore (Milik), hoax (Gaster); scholars disagree whether it was real
